html:
Saint Kitts and Nevis became independent from Britain on 19 September 1983, the smallest country in the Americas by area and people. Kennedy Simmonds was the first prime minister.

The new state followed the breakaway of Anguilla and the end of the old three island colony. Its constitution gave Nevis its own assembly and the right to secede; a vote in 1998 to leave fell short of the two thirds needed.

St Kitts closed its state sugar industry in 2005 after more than three centuries, and turned to tourism. Its programme selling citizenship for investment, begun in 1984, is the oldest in the world and a large source of income for the Commonwealth state.
